before_objects.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
before_objects.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Field class] The fields admitted with singular sources are the locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, and, for the sheet case, the pairs that are $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$ for each $t$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]); for such a field $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes the jump of the one-sided traces.

(e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume fields of [[def-em-sources]] and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This is the precise content of the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] extended to the point and stationary-sheet sources defined here.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition.
before_objects.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) fixes the field class: locally integrable for the pairings, and $C^1$ off the sheet with one-sided $C^1$ traces exactly for the interface formulas of the page's jump theorem whose hypotheses cite this definition. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition.

before_objects.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
before_objects.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and every distributional source pair, including source types defined by their own pairings, for which the four equations hold. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. No choice principle is used in this item.
before_objects.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows.

before_objects.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
before_objects.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$ at every $t\in I$, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.
before_objects.strategy:
Assume the fields of the statement. Because $S$ is stationary, the interface formula of [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] applies to the spatial divergence and curl of each field at each time, with the same normal convention $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$ and jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$ as fixed in [[def-em-surface-distribution]] and [[def-em-weak-sources]](c); in particular
$$\operatorname{div}E=\{\operatorname{div}E\}+n\cdot[E]\,\delta_{S\times I},\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\{\operatorname{curl}B\}+n\times[B]\,\delta_{S\times I}$$
as distributions on $U$, where $\{\ \}$ denotes the locally integrable function equal to the classical divergence or curl on each open side, and $\delta_{S\times I}$ is the functional $\psi\mapsto\int_I\int_S\psi\,dS\,dt$ built from the sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c).

First separate the ordinary from the singular parts. Restrict the pairing of the weak Gauss law $\operatorname{div}E=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0+\rho_S/\varepsilon_0$ to test functions supported in $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$: the singular term vanishes, so $\int_{(\Omega\setminus S)\times I}(\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0)\psi=0$ for every such test function. The function $g:=\{\operatorname{div}E\}-\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the open set $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and its integral against every test function supported there vanishes; such a continuous $g$ vanishes identically, because if $g(p)\ne0$ one chooses a ball around $p$ on which $g$ has one sign with $|g|\ge|g(p)|/2$ and a nonnegative bump supported in it with positive integral ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]), contradicting the vanishing by [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. Hence $\{\operatorname{div}E\}=\rho_v/\varepsilon_0$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$, and subtracting the resulting identity from the weak equation leaves
$$(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\,\delta_{S\times I}=0.$$
Testing with $\psi(x,t)=\varphi(x)\eta(t)$, $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$, and using that the inner integral is continuous in $t$ gives $\int_I\eta(t)\int_S\bigl(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0\bigr)\varphi\,dS\,dt=0$ for all $\eta$; the function $F(t):=\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS$ is continuous on $I$, and a continuous function on an interval whose integral against every compactly supported test vanishes is identically zero, by the same one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); hence $F(t)=0$ for every $t\in I$, that is, $\int_S(n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0)\varphi\,dS=0$ at every $t\in I$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); the surface density $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on the compact $S$ at each such $t$, so [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] gives $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $S\times I$. Repeating the same two-step argument — off-sheet vanishing by the sign-and-bump localization, then surface localization — with the other three weak equations:
- from $\operatorname{div}B=0$ (no volume magnetic source and no magnetic sheet term): $n\cdot[B]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, whose right side is represented by the locally integrable function $-\partial_tB$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with no delta part because the interface is stationary and $B$ has one-sided $C^1$ traces: $n\times[E]=0$ on $S\times I$;
- from $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_v+c^{-2}\partial_tE+\mu_0J_S$, where $J_S$ is the sheet functional with density $K$: $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$ on $S\times I$, which is exactly $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}n\times[B]$ since $n\times[B]$ is tangential.
All hypotheses used are those stated: the one-sided $C^1$ traces make the interface formula applicable ([[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]), continuity of $\rho_v,J_v$ on the open complement makes the sign-and-bump localization applicable there, and continuity of the traces and of $\sigma,K$ makes [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] applicable. The marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the interface and surface-measure items; no further choice is used.

before_objects.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
before_objects.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], $I$ an open interval ([[def-interval]]), with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the source fields of [[def-em-sources]]; put $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and define the two Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$$
with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds. Then
$$\partial_tD_B=0,\qquad \partial_tD_E=0$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$. Consequently, for every fixed $x\in\Omega$, the functions $t\mapsto D_B(x,t)$ and $t\mapsto D_E(x,t)$ are constant on the interval $I$: if the two Gauss constraints hold at one time $t_0\in I$, that is $D_B(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $D_E(\cdot,t_0)=0$, then they hold at every $t\in I$; and if a defect is nonzero at one time it is nonzero, with the same value, at every time.

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and suppose the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds; let $D_B=\operatorname{div}B$ and $D_E=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ be the resulting distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). Then
$$\partial_tD_B=0,\qquad \partial_tD_E=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. Moreover, if $D_B$ and $D_E$ are represented by continuous functions on $\Omega\times I$, then those functions are independent of $t$ (this clause uses the Lebesgue-integral interface with its declared Countable Choice convention, [[def-countable-choice]]); hence a defect that vanishes at one time vanishes at every time, and a nonzero defect persists.

The theorem identifies the exact content of 'the evolution equations preserve the Gauss constraints': it is the combination of the divergence-of-curl identity with the continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]], and it asserts no existence of fields and no measurement.
before_objects.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. Since $B$ is $C^2$, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] gives $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$. Taking the divergence of Faraday's law and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) gives $\partial_t\operatorname{div}B=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0$, the interchange of the time and space derivatives being [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] applied to the $C^2$ components of $B$. For the electric defect, $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=-\operatorname{div}\partial_tE=\operatorname{div}\bigl(c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J\bigr)=-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J$ using Amp\`ere's law and $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$; and $\partial_t(\rho/\varepsilon_0)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$ with $\rho$ of class $C^1$. Hence $\partial_tD_E=-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0$, where $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the last equality is the continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). For fixed $x$, the functions $t\mapsto D_B(x,t)$ and $t\mapsto D_E(x,t)$ are differentiable on the interval $I$ with vanishing derivative, so [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] gives constancy on $I$, proving both the propagation and the persistence clause.

(b) Distributional branch. The same computations hold with distributional derivatives: [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] gives the commutation $\partial_t\partial_iB_i=\partial_i\partial_tB_i$ and the vanishing of $\sum_i\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ (the two reindexed sums are negatives of each other), and linearity of the pairing gives $\partial_tD_B=0$ and, with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ and the distributional continuity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), $\partial_tD_E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. For the propagation clause, suppose $D_B$, say, is represented by a continuous function $h$ on $U$; then for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ the function $F(t):=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)\,d\lambda_3(x)$ is continuous on $I$, and for every $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\eta=0$ the product $\psi:=\varphi\eta$ is the time derivative of the compactly supported function $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)\int_{t_0}^t\eta$ ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] supplies the bumps needed to write any such $\eta$; the construction is the standard vanishing-fibre-integral test), so $0=\langle\partial_th,\psi\rangle=-\int_I F\eta$. Choosing once and for all a bump $\beta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ with $\int_I\beta=1$, writing an arbitrary test $\eta$ as $\eta-(\int\eta)\beta+(\int\eta)\beta$ and applying the previous identity to the part with vanishing integral shows that the functional $\eta\mapsto\int_IF\eta$ is a constant multiple of $\int\eta$; hence $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for all $\eta$ with $C:=\int_IF\beta$. The continuous function $F-C$ vanishes identically: if $F(t_0)\ne C$, take a subinterval on which $F-C$ has one sign with $|F-C|\ge|F(t_0)-C|/2$ and a nonnegative bump supported in it with positive integral ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]), contradicting the vanishing by [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. As $\varphi$ was arbitrary, $h(\cdot,t_1)=h(\cdot,t_2)$ on $\Omega$ for all $t_1,t_2\in I$, by the same sign-and-bump argument applied in the spatial variable ([[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]). This proves independence of $t$, and the propagation and persistence clauses follow. The marked Countable Choice belongs only to this Lebesgue-integral localization clause; the algebraic parts of both branches are choice-free.

before_objects.title: A suddenly appearing point charge with zero current is inadmissible
before_objects.statement:
Let $q\ne0$ be a real charge parameter (coulombs) and let $U:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the laboratory conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. Define a distribution $\rho$ on $U$ by
$$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_0^\infty\psi(0,t)\,dt,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$$
— the point-source pairing of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) for the constant trajectory $z(t)=0$ on $I_0=(0,\infty)$, with the endpoint term omitted — and let $J:=0$ be the zero distribution. Then:

(a) $\partial_t\rho=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}$ and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), hence $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}\ne0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$: for every test function $\psi$, $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\,\psi(0,0)$, because $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth with compact support. In particular the continuity identity fails at the appearance event $(0,0)$.

(b) Consequently there are no locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $U$ satisfying the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,0)$ in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e): such fields would satisfy the distributional continuity identity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), which (a) contradicts. The source pair $(\rho,0)$ is therefore not a source pair of the declared weak Maxwell model.

(c) The failure is exactly the omitted endpoint term of the point-source construction: by the endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]], the same trajectory on a bounded interval $I_0=(a,b)$ has $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$ with $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$. A switched point charge with $J=0$ and no endpoint or current term is thus inadmissible; a switched charge must be accompanied by an explicit current or endpoint source term, which the weak equations of [[def-em-weak-sources]] then require to satisfy continuity.

This is a mathematical incompatibility statement about a declared source model, not a report of a measurement: no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical claim is involved.
before_objects.strategy: Direct computation with the distributional definitions. (a) For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$ the pullback $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth and compactly supported, so $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-\langle\rho,\partial_t\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\psi(0,0)$ by the fundamental theorem of calculus on the support interval ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); the functional $\psi\mapsto q\psi(0,0)$ is $q\delta_{(0,0)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), which is nonzero because $q\ne0$ and some test function equals $1$ at $(0,0)$. Since $J$ is the zero distribution, $\operatorname{div}J=0$. (b) If locally integrable fields $E,B$ satisfied the four weak equations in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the distributional pair $(\rho,0)$, then [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) — stated for arbitrary distributional source pairs satisfying the four equations — would give $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$, contradicting (a). (c) The endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] computes the endpoint deltas of a finite-history point source; setting $J=0$ while retaining the charge history $(0,\infty)$ is precisely the omission of those endpoint terms. Nothing here is a physical claim about charge creation: it states that the declared source model fails its own continuity requirement, and it exhibits the general statement of the previous item on an explicit example. The item inherits the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-em-weak-sources]], on whose clause (b) it depends, and records it in its dependencies; the computation itself is choice-free and uses neither the surface-measure interface nor any selection.

proposed_subjects.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
proposed_subjects.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Unrestricted weak fields and optional interface branches] The general field class for the solution predicate (e) consists of all locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, also when the source has a stationary-sheet part. No classical one-sided trace or off-sheet $C^1$ regularity is required to define those four distributional pairings. Additional trace hypotheses are optional hypotheses of interface/jump results, not admission requirements of the general weak model.
For a pointwise classical jump branch, one may additionally assume that $E,B$ are $C^1$ off $S\times I$ and, around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighborhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. These joint one-sided extensions make the field traces and first spatial/temporal derivatives continuous up to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders.
For the broader weak-trace branch, one may instead assume the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, with the explicit additional conditions that the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ for $dSdt$. This branch supports sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jump identities; spatial continuity at each time gives pointwise spatial identities for almost every time, and joint continuity of the jump densities gives the further all-time upgrade. Separate spatial $C^1$ traces at each time alone do not imply that joint regularity or upgrade. Whenever such traces exist, $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes their jump in the chosen normal convention. (e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume densities with the charge/current quantity types of [[def-em-sources]] (the weak predicate requires this stated $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity, not the classical continuous-source regularity) and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This clause defines a solution predicate. When the singular parts vanish, its four identities are the same as the locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. That earlier postulate explicitly excludes point and sheet distributions and does not imply their physical adoption here; adoption for the declared singular-source models is made separately, after this definition. No physical field equation is deduced merely from defining this predicate.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition.
proposed_subjects.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) retains the unrestricted locally integrable field pair for the weak predicate, including sheet sources. It records optional interface hypotheses separately: joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions support the pointwise branch; the weaker per-time spatial C1 trace branch needs the explicit piecewise-derivative and sheet-trace L1 hypotheses for its distribution/a.e. conclusions. Neither branch is a general weak-field admission condition, and separate spatial C1 traces alone are not claimed to give joint continuity or temporal bounds. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition. The vanishing-pairing clause is a precise mathematical solution predicate. It agrees with the old postulate on its original locally integrable source class, but does not extend that physical postulate deductively to singular sources; physical adoption is a separate postulate. It remains possible for a declared source pair to be incompatible with those equations, and no existence is asserted.

proposed_subjects.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
proposed_subjects.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the original locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source/field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the Countable Choice assumption of its defining source/surface-measure formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
proposed_subjects.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

proposed_subjects.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
proposed_subjects.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade.
proposed_subjects.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, cover its intersection with $S\times I$ by finitely many smaller stationary graph cylinders, and use [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]] to reduce to tests supported in one such cylinder or away from $S$. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used.

Pointwise classical jumps use the explicit joint one-sided regularity or an independently established jointly continuous jump; the specified locally integrable trace branch gives sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jumps. The unrestricted L1 weak framework does not by itself define pointwise classical traces. Physical adoption for the declared stationary-sheet sources is the separate distributional-source Maxwell postulate, and the original L1-only postulate is not applied outside its source domain.

proposed_subjects.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
proposed_subjects.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$ ([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$
(a) Smooth evolution branch. Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$ $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only the two evolution equations
$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$
and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise. For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero initial Gauss defect.
(b) Distributional evolution branch. The same derivative conclusion holds for arbitrary scalar/vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in $\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This includes the original locally integrable field/source branch identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$, assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral/localization interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is assumed.
(c) Full-Maxwell corollaries. Smooth solutions of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally-integrable weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point/stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise in (a) and distributionally in (b).
This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the continuous-representative localization and inherited declared singular-source formulation.
proposed_subjects.strategy:
(a) Smooth algebra. For $C^2$ fields, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] give
$$\partial_tD_B=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tB)=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0,$$
and, with the positive commutation sign,
$$\partial_tD_E=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=c^2\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0.$$
Here $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the final equality is the separately assumed continuity, not a consequence of the evolution equations alone. The coordinate operators and product/linear rules are [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For fixed $x$, [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on compact subintervals of $I$ proves constancy, propagation and nonzero persistence.
(b) The identical componentwise cancellation holds for distributions by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], whose derivative-commutation clause is choice-free: in $\sum_{i,j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ the exchanged $i,j$ terms cancel. The two evolution identities and the independent continuity identity therefore give $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ without multiplying distributions.
For the continuous-representative conclusion, assume the stated Countable Choice and let $\partial_th=0$. Fix a spatial test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and put $F(t)=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)d\lambda_3(x)$. On any compact time subinterval the integrands have fixed compact spatial support and a uniform bound, by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]] and [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. Hence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] makes $F$ continuous. All products with compact temporal tests are absolutely integrable; [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify their multiple integrals with $\int_I F\eta$.
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ has zero integral, extend it by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)dv$. Equivalently start at a point strictly left of its support. The compact-test integral agrees with its Riemann integral by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] gives $H\prime=\eta$. Since the total integral is zero, $H$ vanishes both left and right of the support interval; it is smooth and compactly supported inside $I$. Therefore $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a legitimate compact test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$. Apply the derivative equation to THIS primitive test:
$$0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_I F(t)\eta(t)dt.$$
Choose a real nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ in $I$ with integral one, using [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] and the positive finite measure of an inner interval ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Decompose an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta_0=\eta-(\int_I\eta)\beta$. The preceding equality gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for every $\eta$, where $C:=\int_IF\beta$. A continuous function with all such pairings zero vanishes pointwise: if a real or imaginary component is nonzero, continuity gives a subinterval where that component has one sign and is bounded away from zero; a nonnegative bump supported there, equal to one on a smaller interval, contradicts integral monotonicity ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Thus $F$ is constant. The same argument for the continuous spatial difference $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$, now using bumps in $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, shows it is identically zero, since its pairing with every $\varphi$ is zero. This establishes independence of time. Compact support of every test, the actual derivative-test slot, and the public Countable Choice cost are explicit; no arbitrary-basepoint primitive is used.
(c) In the smooth full-Maxwell branch, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] supplies continuity, while Gauss gives $D_B=D_E=0$ directly; the original weak branch is the identical distributional argument. The separately adopted singular-source postulate uses the preceding solution predicate and the distributional continuity result. Conversely the propagated zero defects are exactly the missing two Gauss identities, so adding them to the evolution pair yields all four equations. No existence or empirical claim is inferred.

proposed_subjects.title: A suddenly appearing point charge with zero current is inadmissible
proposed_subjects.statement:
Let $q\ne0$ be a real charge parameter (coulombs) and let $U:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the laboratory conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. Define a distribution $\rho$ on $U$ by
$$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_0^\infty\psi(0,t)\,dt,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$$
— an explicit switched-history distribution for $z(t)=0$ on $(0,\infty)$, with no compensating current or source contribution at the appearance event; it does not satisfy the proper-graph hypothesis of the zero-endpoint continuity branch of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) — and let $J:=0$ be the zero distribution. Then:

(a) $\partial_t\rho=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}$ and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), hence $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}\ne0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$: for every test function $\psi$, $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\,\psi(0,0)$, because $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth with compact support. In particular the continuity identity fails at the appearance event $(0,0)$.

(b) Consequently there are no locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $U$ satisfying the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,0)$ in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e): such fields would satisfy the distributional continuity identity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), which (a) contradicts. The source pair $(\rho,0)$ is therefore incompatible even with the formal four residual identities, and cannot be an actual source/field model under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]].

(c) The failure is exactly the omitted endpoint term of the point-source construction: by the endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]], the same trajectory on a bounded interval $I_0=(a,b)$ has $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$ with $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$. A switched point charge with $J=0$ and no endpoint or current term is thus inadmissible; a switched charge must be accompanied by an explicit current or endpoint source term, which the weak equations of [[def-em-weak-sources]] then require to satisfy continuity.

This is a mathematical incompatibility statement about a declared source model, not a report of a measurement: no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical claim is involved.
proposed_subjects.strategy: Direct computation with the distributional definitions. (a) For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$ the pullback $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth and compactly supported, so $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-\langle\rho,\partial_t\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\psi(0,0)$ by the fundamental theorem of calculus on the support interval ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); the functional $\psi\mapsto q\psi(0,0)$ is $q\delta_{(0,0)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), which is nonzero because $q\ne0$ and some test function equals $1$ at $(0,0)$. Since $J$ is the zero distribution, $\operatorname{div}J=0$. (b) If locally integrable fields $E,B$ satisfied the four weak equations in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the distributional pair $(\rho,0)$, then [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) — stated for arbitrary distributional source pairs satisfying the four equations — would give $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$, contradicting (a). (c) The endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] computes the endpoint deltas of a finite-history point source; setting $J=0$ while retaining the charge history $(0,\infty)$ is precisely the omission of those endpoint terms. Nothing here is a physical claim about charge creation: it states that the declared source model fails its own continuity requirement, and it exhibits the general statement of the previous item on an explicit example. The item inherits the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-em-weak-sources]], on whose clause (b) it depends, and records it in its dependencies; the computation itself is choice-free and uses neither the surface-measure interface nor any selection. The adopted physical singular-source equations are now supplied by [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; the original weak postulate excludes singular densities. The nonexistence proof is stronger than any source-admission question, since the four formal residual identities themselves imply the continuity that the switched history violates.

additional_same_A_items.design_state: necessary-physical-adoption-interface; proposal with source-backed nonproof formulation
additional_same_A_items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared distributional/surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
are required in $\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning that all four residual pairings defined there vanish for every compact smooth test.
